feed.title: DevOps & Infrastructure — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Ansible
entry.summary: Agentless configuration management and automation that provisions servers with YAML playbooks.

entry.title: Argo
entry.summary: A suite of Kubernetes-native workflow and GitOps continuous-delivery tools (Argo CD, Workflows).

entry.title: Awesome Actions
entry.summary: A list of ready actions for GitHub Actions, automating your workflow.

entry.title: Awesome Ansible
entry.summary: A list of roles and resources for Ansible, the Python-based IT configuration tool.

entry.title: Awesome Backstage
entry.summary: A resource list for Backstage, building internal developer portals.

entry.title: Awesome CDK
entry.summary: A resource list for the AWS CDK, defining infrastructure with real code.

entry.title: Awesome Kubernetes
entry.summary: A list of tools, tutorials and production experience for the Kubernetes ecosystem. Unlike the official docs it gathers community tools and real-world patterns together.

entry.title: Awesome Nix
entry.summary: A list of tools, libraries and guides for the Nix package manager and NixOS. Unlike general Linux lists it focuses on reproducible, declarative configuration.

entry.title: Awesome OpenTofu
entry.summary: A resource list for OpenTofu, the open-source fork of Terraform.

entry.title: Awesome Prometheus
entry.summary: A list of exporters and resources for Prometheus, the open-source monitoring system.

entry.title: Awesome Splunk
entry.summary: A resource list for Splunk, the log-search and monitoring platform.

entry.title: Awesome Terraform
entry.summary: A list of modules and resources for Terraform, managing infrastructure as code.

entry.title: Chaos Mesh
entry.summary: A cloud-native, Kubernetes-integrated chaos-engineering (fault-injection) platform.

entry.title: Cloudflare
entry.summary: Infrastructure offering CDN, DNS, DDoS protection and edge computing in one platform. Unlike separate services it unites them in one dashboard with a generous free tier.

entry.title: Earthly
entry.summary: A build-automation tool giving repeatable builds that behave the same locally and in CI.

entry.title: Harbor
entry.summary: A private container-image registry with security scanning and access control.

entry.title: Helm
entry.summary: A package manager that packages and deploys Kubernetes applications as charts.

entry.title: JitPack
entry.summary: Makes GitHub repos that don’t publish jars usable directly as dependencies.

entry.title: K9s
entry.summary: A fast, interactive terminal UI for managing Kubernetes clusters.

entry.title: Kubernetes
entry.summary: The official site of the open-source system that deploys, manages and heals containers at scale.

entry.title: OpenTofu
entry.summary: A community-driven open-source fork of Terraform that runs the same configurations.

entry.title: Pants
entry.summary: A build system that scales to large, multi-language monorepos (originated at Twitter).

entry.title: Portainer
entry.summary: A self-hosted tool that manages Docker and Kubernetes environments through a visual UI.

entry.title: Prometheus
entry.summary: An open-source monitoring system for metrics collection and alerting, with a time-series database.

entry.title: Terraform
entry.summary: HashiCorp's tool to define and provision infrastructure as code, managing cloud resources declaratively.

entry.title: CNCF Sertifikasyon
entry.summary: Kubernetes certifications through CKA, CKAD and CKS. Unlike cloud provider certificates they are vendor-neutral, and the exam happens at a terminal — not multiple choice, but tasks solved on a live cluster.

entry.title: Cronmaster
entry.summary: A self-hosted web interface for cron jobs that renders expressions in readable form and keeps a run log. Against `crontab -e` it shows the next run time and the last output, which makes silently failing jobs visible.

entry.title: Crontab Generator
entry.summary: Builds a cron expression from a form and states in words when it will fire. Against crontab.guru it runs the other way: instead of decoding an expression, it produces one from the schedule you describe.

entry.title: FromLatest
entry.summary: Analyses a Dockerfile, explains what happens layer by layer and suggests improvements. Against hadolint it is visual and states why each rule exists, which makes it usable for learning to write Dockerfiles rather than only linting them.

entry.title: K8s YAML Generator
entry.summary: Generates Kubernetes manifests from a form, explaining each field beside it. Against copying from the docs you leave with a valid manifest and pick up what the fields mean on the way.

entry.title: ShellCheck
entry.summary: A static analyser for shell scripts that finds unquoted variables, wrong test syntax and portability traps. Against `bash -n` it checks meaning rather than syntax, so it catches the script that runs and misbehaves.

entry.title: YAMLlint
entry.summary: A YAML validator that surfaces indentation and quoting errors and prints the parsed document back. Against a JSON validator it catches YAML’s actual trap: indentation that silently produces the wrong structure.

entry.title: Njalla
entry.summary: Registers the domain in its own name on your behalf, so you do not appear in WHOIS. Unlike a privacy proxy the legal ownership sits with them, which makes it a question of trust.

entry.title: AlexHost
entry.summary: Moldova-based hosting chosen for a different jurisdiction and looser content policy — which also raises the question of who your neighbours are.

entry.title: AvenaCloud
entry.summary: A VPS and dedicated server provider positioned on budget for small-scale projects.

entry.title: Amazon Web Services
entry.summary: The cloud with the widest service range. The breadth is an advantage, while cost tracking is its own discipline — egress charges in particular catch people out.

entry.title: Apache Airflow
entry.summary: An orchestrator scheduling data pipelines as Python-defined directed graphs (DAGs). Unlike cron it offers dependencies, retries and visibility into historical runs.

entry.title: Coder
entry.summary: Runs development environments as containers on your own infrastructure, reached from a VS Code or JetBrains client. Against GitHub Codespaces it is not tied to a cloud provider — both the compute and the code stay with you.

entry.title: Kestra
entry.summary: Flows are declared in YAML, and being language-agnostic it works for teams that are not on Python. It sits well in version control.

entry.title: Make
entry.summary: Scenarios carry branching, loops and error handling, which makes complex flows easier than Zapier’s linear steps. The learning curve is correspondingly steeper.
